guide.summary: Museums, a royal palace, a medieval church and a riverside lookout, with breakfast cafés, bakeries, a food hall, dinners and a cocktail bar checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Book the Anne Frank House early: tickets are sold only online for a set time slot, released every Tuesday at 10am for visits six weeks later, and none are sold at the door.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Eye Filmmuseum's exhibition is closed on Mondays outside school holidays, and NEMO Science Museum opens only on listed Mondays such as 26 October and 2 November 2026. Hartog's Volkoren is closed on Sundays, and the Oude Kerk is temporarily closed 9-12 November.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: The Rijksmuseum requires a booked start time, including for Museumkaart holders, and NEMO tickets also have a start time. Anne Frank House tickets are online only and cannot be exchanged or refunded.

toolkit.label: Walk-in or queue
toolkit.copy: Little Collins is walk-in only, De Wasserette says reservations are not necessary, and Bakers & Roasters works mainly walk-in with a virtual waitlist (limited reservations at Kadijksplein only). Super Lyan takes no reservations except for groups of more than 8.

toolkit.label: Bags and payment
toolkit.copy: The Stedelijk Museum does not allow backpacks or weekend cases in the galleries, and the Royal Palace allows only small bags up to 30x30x15 cm. Eye Filmmuseum and the Anne Frank House take card payments only.

guide.dek: Book your timed museum slots first, then build mornings around the walk-in brunch cafés and evenings around a reserved dinner.
intro: Amsterdam's headline museums run on timed entry, so plan those first. The Rijksmuseum on Museumstraat is open daily from 9 to 17h, including public holidays, and says booking a start time is required. Its current shows include Willem de Kooning at work, on until 17 January, while Carel Visser's sculptures in the museum gardens end on 25 October. The Anne Frank House at Westermarkt 20 sells tickets only online for a fixed slot, releasing them every Tuesday at 10am for visits six weeks ahead, so you should book as early as you can.

On Museumplein, the Stedelijk Museum is open daily from 10am to 6pm, with last entry at 5.45pm. Yayoi Kusama runs from 11 September 2026 to 17 January 2027, alongside Adam Pendleton's Some Wild Kind of Language from 10 October. Leave your backpack behind, as backpacks are not allowed in the galleries. The Royal Palace on Dam Square is open to visitors from 1 October to 11 November, from 10am on calendar days, though it may close for royal events. Nearby, the Oude Kerk opens Mire Lee: Vomit My Blessing on 13 November.

Across the IJ, Eye Filmmuseum shows an Ulrich Seidl exhibition from 19 September 2026 to 31 January 2027; its exhibition is closed on Mondays outside school holidays. Next door, A'DAM Lookout is open daily from 10:00 to 22:00, with last admission at 21:00, and knocks €2 off tickets when you book online. If you travel with children, NEMO Science Museum at Oosterdok 2 sells tickets with a start time and suggests weekdays after 14:00 as quieter. ARTIS has reopened its restored aquarium and offers a €15 weekday late-afternoon ticket from 16:00.

For food, many places are walk-in. Little Collins in De Pijp serves brunch daily from 9 to 16, walk-in only, and De Wasserette opens daily from 7:30 to 17:00 without reservations. Bakers & Roasters runs two branches with a virtual waitlist. For dinner, Cafe de Klepel on Prinsenstraat takes bookings up to two months ahead, for tables of up to 8. Foodhallen is open daily from 12:00 to 23:00, and Super Lyan pours cocktails from 17:00 Wednesday to Sunday with no reservations for small groups.
summaryCards: Book a Rijksmuseum start time and an online Anne Frank House slot, then add the Royal Palace on Dam Square while it is open until 11 November.
Walk in for brunch at Little Collins or De Wasserette, then pick up bread at Hartog's Volkoren on Wibautstraat, which is closed on Sundays.
Check closing days: Eye's exhibition shuts on Mondays outside school holidays, NEMO opens only on listed Mondays, and the Oude Kerk closes 9-12 November.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several official sites could not be read by automated fetch: De Kas and the City of Amsterdam pages for Vondelpark and Albert Cuyp Market (HTTP 403), Restaurant Breda and Dignita (503 or connection refused), Lot Sixty One and Hortus Botanicus (certificate errors), the Van Gogh Museum (no readable content), and the GVB ferry page (403). Tales & Spirits' domain redirects elsewhere and Door 74's site is under construction. Some places were published only partially: NEMO and ARTIS hours were not readable, the Rembrandt House Museum's closing time was cut off, the Royal Palace's daily calendar did not load, and several cafés and bakeries (Cafe de Klepel, Little Collins, Fabel Friet, Hartog's Volkoren, Bocca Coffee, De Wasserette) showed hours but no 2026-dated content, so they are marked medium confidence. Gap candidates checked exceeded eight because many failed; the confirmed total is 22, below the 25-35 target.
